 Game Analysis , Pre-Game Gameday: Wizards @ Raptors, November 18th
 Another chance to snap the losing streak
 November 18, 2026 Matthew Mountjoy The good news is the Raps don’t have to worry about the Knicks tonight. However, the Washington Wizards have rolled into town, and both teams have plenty of reasons to try and win this one and get the monkey off their back. While the Raptors have lost five straight, the Wizards’ losing streak has reached eight games.
 The Raptors could easily win this game—and you can say that about many of their losses so far this season. Even in the last two games, The Raps have jumped out to a sizeable lead against a very strong team early, lost the momentum, failed to lock it down, and then lost the game.
 For the Raps, it’s an opportunity to snap the streak and build momentum with the starters returning from Injury. For the Wizards, it’s an opportunity to finally get back in the win column.
 Raptors Outlook 
 Record: 5-9 (tied for 9th in the Eastern Conference)
 Offensive Rating: 114.1 (14th)
 Defensive Rating: 113.3 (15th)
 Net Rating: 0.8 (15th)
 Raptors previous results: 111-102 L to New York Knicks
 The Raptors repeated history once again on Tuesday night, falling to the Knicks 111-102 in regulation. With Scottie Barnes now back in the mix, and guys like Allen Graves, Jamal Shead, and Ja’Kobe Walter proving their effectiveness with insanely strong play this season, I’m hoping that an expected strong start and the defensive qualities that we’ve seen from the Raps can outweigh a Wizards team that’s hungry for results.

 Wizards Outlook 
 Record: 4-11 (12th in the Eastern Conference)
 Offensive Rating: 109.9 (25th)
 Defensive Rating: 117.6 (26th)
 Net Rating: -7.8 (25th)
 Wizards’ previous results: 136-120 L to Memphis Grizzlies
 This Wizards squad has a litany of problems this season, with a major point being the defence and rebounding. Their abysmal -7.8 net rating ranks 25th this season, despite the fact that they currently employ both Anthony Davis and Deandre Ayton. They have had good offensive games this season (see: 144-140 loss to the Pistons, and the 128-116 win over the Bucks), but against a Raptors team that excels at rebounding, that could be trouble.
